{{RaceIcon|Worgen}} [[Worgen]] |boss= {{NPC||Archmage Arugal|icon=Human Male}} |level= 18-24 |minlevel= 10 |players= 5 |bosses= {{Shadowfang Keep}} }} '''Shadowfang Keep''', formerly known as '''Silverlaine Keep''',[[The Silverpine Wars]] is a haunted keep in southern [[Silverpine Forest]], near [[Pyrewood Village]]. It is the base of operations for the evil archmage [[Arugal]] and his [[worgen]] progeny. ==History== From the [https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Game_Guide/World_Dungeons World Dungeons] page on the official World of Warcraft Community Site: :''During the [[Third War]], the wizards of the [[Kirin Tor]] battled against the undead armies of the [[Scourge]]. When the wizards of [[Dalaran]] died in battle, they would rise soon after - adding their former might to the growing Scourge. Frustrated by their lack of progress (and against the advice of his peers) the [[Archmage]], [[Arugal]] elected to summon extra-dimensional entities to bolster Dalaran's diminishing ranks. Arugal's summoning brought the ravenous worgen into the world of [[Azeroth]]. The feral wolf-men slaughtered not only the Scourge, but quickly turned on the wizards themselves. The worgen sieged the keep of the noble, [[Baron Silverlaine]]. Situated above the tiny hamlet of [[Pyrewood]], the keep quickly fell into shadow and ruin. Driven mad with guilt, Arugal adopted the worgen as his children and retreated to the newly dubbed 'Shadowfang Keep'. It's said he still resides there, protected by his massive pet, Fenrus - and haunted by the vengeful ghost of Baron Silverlaine.'' Pyrewood Village is shadowed to the north by Shadowfang Keep, once a bastion of [[Alliance]] power but now the dark residence of a mad former [[mage]] of the [[Kirin Tor]], named Arugal. The worgen that stalk the Keep, as well as the cursed villagers of Pyrewood, are the doings of this madman. During the Third War, Arugal made these worgen as allies but they could not be controlled and turned on him and the other soldiers. He went mad after this and now accepts them as his "children." His worgen run rampant throughout much of the forest. [[Jordan Stilwell]] and [[Daphne Stilwell]] used to live and work here before the Third War. During the events of World of Warcraft, agents of the Banshee Queen [[Sylvanas Windrunner]] were dispatched to both solve the mystery of the enigmatic worgen and ultimately terminate the source of the creatures' infestation in Silverpine. Shadow Hunter Jasta is honored as a Champion of Darkspear Tribe, for his contribution to his own tribe and to the Horde. He is one of Vol'jin's chosen champion to act in his command to lead the Trolls organization the Vol'jin's Headhunters.

He led a crew on an invasion plan into the Echo Isles, but soon after some time, he was cursed by a powerful spell, a voodoo of Zalazane, which trapped him in the spiritual world for a long time and his body was asleep in Thrall's Fortress.

Jasta is a veteran of the Darkspear tribe, completely loyal to the Horde. His legacy is preserved in Sen'jin Village and Orgrimmar.

After his life in Durotar, Jasta began wandering across Azeroth alone, silently safeguarding his troll brothers. While he is down for the Horde, as a Shadow Hunter he maintain balance and neutrality instead of direct hostility. Channeling the power of the Loa, he uses his blessings to defend his people and keep the peace by deleting threats with no hesitation.

While Jasta walks his solitary path, his two apprentices—Wol-kree and Wol the Axe Dancer—stay at his secret base. Having been trained by Jasta himself, they remain behind in hiding, always waiting for their master's return.

Following the fall of the Second Gurubashi Empire, Jasta took Wol the Axe Dancer and sent him back to this secret sanctuary, a place known to no one but Jasta, his companions, and the loas.

== Journey of Jasta ==
# '''In a Valley somewhere in Durotar''' - A fleet of Kul'Tiran humans arrived on Durotar after some time of quiet, and they began to threaten the Horde members near their encampment, A hunter from the Darkspear Tribe named Jasta decides to fight for his homeland and people, he begins to undergo the trials of becoming a horde warrior. he is one of his tribe's bravest hunters.
# '''Durotar & Sen'jin Village''' - Jasta completed the Trials and is now on his way to Sen'jin Village to do some quests, He found that fighting demons and other unusual creatures was not as easy as he thought it would be, but nevertheless he persisted through it all. This was Jasta's first time entering the Valley of Trials, so by completing these challenges he learned a lot and improved his skills in combat and he is now prepared to go to his next journey that awaits him in Durotar.
# '''Durotar & Echo Isles''' - After completing his work in Sen'jin Village, Jasta was informed by Master Gadrin that he was prepared and ready to join the horde troops stationed at Razor Hill for the protection of Durotar. Upon arriving there, Jasta met with high-ranking members of the Razor Hill forces who assigned him a mission to Thunder Ridge, Jasta fought the gigantic thunder lizards, and other dangerous animals through the deserts of Durotar, while going back to Razor Hill he encountered two Kul Tiran Marines near a destroyed keep, he ended up getting attacked but he survived and defeated the humans using his insane aim, despite being unfamiliar with the area, Jasta successfully completed the task without any hard struggles. He then returned to Razor Hill carrying two severed human heads which are the Kul Tiran Marines' heads, the orcs were impressed by his skills and didn't hesitate to put him into their ranks as a ranged soldier. Since that time when Jasta got accepted in the Razor Hill Horde Troops, he now stayed in the Barracks of Razor Hill, now equipped better, ready for war, and earned the title "Headhunter", which is indicative of his identity and skill as a soldier. The troops from Razor Hill were then deployed for this in Echo Isles for an attack on the Kul Tirans. Jasta and the other troops marched to Echo Isles, where they would've immediately started the attack on some small human camps.
# '''Sent to Barrens and tamed a beast''' - Headhunter Jasta was sent to Barrens to do some work there for the Horde, but before he left the Barracks in Razor Hill he told the orc commander to never let the humans salvage his people in Sen'Jin Village. When Jasta arrived at the Barrens, he saw an injured purple raptor and was drawn to it. He approached it cautiously and discovered that it would be valuable to him. he saved the raptor and eventually tamed it. After saving the raptor, Jasta went out to the wilderness to hunt for food together with the raptor, as they spent time together they formed a bond, after the raptor slaughtered many other beasts, Jasta named the raptor "Killa". The creature now serves as his loyal companion, Jasta had fought with the kolkar centaurs and even killed their leaders, he also took down a tough harpy and climbed almost every mountain in the barrens, and fought again with demonic creatures to accomplish his quests for the Horde. Jasta contributed a lot of work to the people of crossroads,  which earned him respect from some guards and civilians in crossroads.
# '''To Thousand Needles''' - After being long enough in the Barrens fighting with Quillboars, Thunder Lizards and Thunder Hawks, Headhunter Jasta feels it is time to move out of the Barrens and explore more lands of Kalimdor. He aims to gain more experience for future battles against threats that the Darkspear and the Horde face, but before that, he been through dangerous missions in Stonetalon Mountains and Ashenvale where he bravely fought with the mysterious night elves that lives there. He travels to Thousand Needles, while Jasta was on his way there, he encountered a Tauren who was seeking help. The Tauren wanted Jasta to kill the dwarves who were destroying their home. Jasta agreed to do so, and went to a dig site of dwarves where there were many destructive machines and dwarves who keeps mining and destroying the place. Jasta took them down one by one until he met the commander. Both had a one on one fight and Jasta won! He took the journal and brought it back to the Tauren. He left the crossroads as an honored one, for everything that he has done for the people of the Horde, and he continues to venture to the Thousand Needles, where he is guided by a spirit's voice.
# '''Back in the Jungle''' - The spirits whispered to Headhunter Jasta again and gave him a vision, stating that he had been chosen. They said they would reveal themselves to him in due time. He also finished all of his tasks and missions in Thousand Needles, he earned honor from the Taurens for all of his efforts. Headhunter Jasta returns to his homeland, where he was born,  Stranglethorn Vale. He goes there because he trusts the spirits who whisper to him. He doesn't know who it is but still believes that it is what he feels and thinks is right, so he continues his journey through the vast jungle with many dangerous creatures but he didn't took Killa with him. He meets a group of hunters in the jungle and joins their party on an expedition into a dangerous part of the jungle, they traveled through this vast wilderness filled with dangerous creatures, he proved himself to be an excellent hunter as well as an excellent member of this group of hunters that is led by a dwarf named "Hemet Nesingwary". Eventually, he succeeds by proving himself and succeeding at what they did not expect from him, he was being able to defeat even the most dangerous creatures in the jungle. Jasta eventually arrived at a Horde base camp, the "Grom'Gol Base Camp". There he found a Troll from his tribe and they began searching for their chieftain's son, Yenniku. Jasta scouted almost every rival tribe's camp but didn't find him yet. The other Trolls in Grom'Gol saw how Jasta infiltrated into his rival's camp and were impressed by his scouting skills. They continued the hunt for Yenniku while Jasta was also looking forward to what would come next in his journey.
# '''Hunting in the Jungle''' - Headhunter Jasta spent his time tracking beasts and hunting with a group of hunters in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, aiding the horde forces in the Grom'Gol base camp and also tracking the son of the chieftain of his tribe. After he had found their chieftain's son, Jasta reported his findings back to Grom'Gol. He knew that he needed to train more to help defeating Zan'Zil and his voodoo slaves, so he decided to train more and ended up in Kargath at Blasted lands, where he was sent on another dangerous hunting mission. He earned honor from the warlord in Kargath for all his efforts for them. At long last, Headhunter Jasta had given his mission in Kargath, he was sent back to Eastern Kingdoms to deliver Neeka Bloodscar's report to the Horde forces in Stonard, Swamp of Sorrows. He also did many works for the Horde forces in Stonard, he was a great help to them and managed to eliminate any threats against the Horde.
# '''Tracking a lost one from the Sanv Tribe''' - Now, as the powerful magic charm called the Sanv Charm is retrieved and given back to the one who owned it who's from the Sanv Tribe, the owner of the Sanv Charm who is called Sanv K'la, asked Headhunter Jasta to report to him if he will ever find the lost Sanv Riftseeker named Akh Z'ador. Akh Z'ador was the one who led the Sanv Draenei tribe to Azeroth. He was one of the few of their kind that knew the magic of their ancient ancestors. He was skilled enough to bring their entire tribe in Azeroth, and that of the Fallow Sanctuary, with the help of the other lesser Riftseekers. Akh Z'ador attempted to return to their old world in search of more exiles to bring to the Harborage. Sanv K'la suspects something went terribly wrong, he could not detect Akh Z'ador's presence upon their old world with the Sanv Charm. the magic he is using is old, and somewhat unstable. They barely understand its usage, and only the bright minds like Akh Z'ador can manipulate it enough to travel. Now while Headhunter Jasta is questing around Azeroth, he will do his best to track down Akh Z'ador
# '''Hunting in the Jungle - 2''' - After wandering around Azeroth seeking experience and combat skills, Headhunter Jasta returns once again to Stranglethorn Vale. Jasta equipped armor from the Grom'Gol Base and went to the ruins where Zanzil and Yenniku reside. Headhunter Jasta infiltrated the ruins and found Yenniku alone. He then strikes at Yenniku as quickly as he can and captures his soul using a mojo, and this is the soul gem. Jasta completes his mission and gains more honor from his tribe. 
# '''First Home''' - Returning to Sen'Jin Village, Headhunter Jasta was about to tell Master Gadrin about his adventure around Azeroth, but Master Gadrin already knew Jasta was going to approach him, so he approached Jasta first. Master Gadrin, seeing a vision of what Jasta had gone through, sent Jasta into First Home to be tested by the loa and become a Shadow Hunter. While in the First Home, Jasta learned enough skills to survive in there, he doesn't know how long he will be there, but when he recalls the time when he entered the Valley of Trials to become a soldier of the Horde and the reason why he took the trials, Jasta gains strength and believes that he will pass the trial and become a Shadow Hunter.
# '''Becoming a Shadow Hunter''' - Jasta survived in First Home; he had no idea how long he had been in the very dark jungle, but he passed and succeeded in his trials; the Loa judged him worthy, so the Loa made him a Shadow Hunter; he was given second sight and can now see and communicate with Loas. While in First Home, Jasta's movements were swift and cunning but cautious; one time he was under a giant jungle leaf that he didn't realize was a Nambu plant, he almost got bitten by the giant carnivorous plant but he dodged away and suddenly had a sense that someone was lurking around him so he lurked behind the giant leaves trying to stalk his stalker, he approached his stalker from the back and tries to tackle it but it turned out it was just a shadowy figure more like a spirit, He chased the shadowy figure until they arrived at a very familiar place, Jasta realizes he is seeing Felwood and finds himself there, seeing green water flowing in the area and bigger threats roaming around, as he looks back, he sees other trolls with him, some of them are also shadow hunters, then Jasta's visions suddenly went all dark and he felt like he was floating like he was meditating, he could feel how calm his body was and can even hear his own heart beat, he had a strong sense of his surroundings, he heard the whispers "You seen da vision, it be future, you a Shadow Hunter now”, he knew that it is the Loa who whispered him, he understood the Loa’s message and accepted his mission that he is to defend the place in the future. After some time, Jasta finds his way out of the First Home jungle, leaving First Home behind as a Shadow Hunter and feeling that some of what he had been through in the jungle was slowly fading from his memories, but he remembered all his lessons and everything he had learned there, especially the Loa's whispers.
# '''Back to Durotar & Sen'jin Village''' - After traveling throughout Azeroth for a long time to gain more skills, and reputations, Shadow Hunter Jasta went back home to show his success to his tribe that he is now a Shadow Hunter, he would stay in the Village for a while to protect his tribespeople from the humans of Anchor's Edge and bring danger to anyone who's a threat to the Darkspear Tribe.
# '''To Amani'alor!''' - Jasta leaves Sen'jin Village together with an old friend who's also a Shadow Hunter, they went to Vol'jin at Grommash Hold in Orgrimmar, they reported the current situation with their tribe and the humans from Anchor's Edge. Arriving in Grommash Hold, the Shadow Hunters told Vol'jin that their Village was fine and the humans haven't caused troubles for a while now. Somehow, the duo noticed a female Forest Troll standing ahead of them, they tried to approach her, they had a talk and then both Shadow Hunters went to the Valley of Honor to equip better armors before going to Valley of Spirits. At Valley of Spirits, they met a female jungle troll who opened a portal for both of them, the portal is to '''Amani'alor''', it is where the Revantusk Trolls and Amani Trolls settled in Kalimdor. Both Shadow Hunters arrived at Amani'alor, wearing capes that has the main color of their tribe's flag, representing the Darkspear pride. They went to the Great Hall in the village and met Warleader Zol'majin, they are welcomed by the Warleader and discussed about their tribes, it ended up both tribes earning great trust to eachother.

The '''Seven Kingdoms''' were the [[human]] states that became sovereign after the disintegration of the [[Arathor|Empire of Arathor]], approximately 1,200 years before the [[First War]].

==History==
The seeds of the kingdoms of men were Arathorian city-states. First among them was [[Strom]], a mighty fortress city of the [[Arathi tribe|Arathi]] tribe located in the regions south of [[Quel'Thalas]]. This bastion became the capital of the nation of [[Arathor]], which saw its number grow as humans from all over the land traveled there to the protection and safety of Strom.<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Arathor_and_the_Troll_Wars Arathor and the Troll Wars]</ref>

After the [[Amani Empire|Amani]] defeat at the end of the [[Troll Wars]] and the death of [[Thoradin]], the Arathorian king, the younger generations of Arathor — then an empire — sought to expand beyond the borders of the lands surrounding the capital. Among them, a group of magi journeyed north because they felt fettered by the strict laws governing magic in Strom. On the southern shore of [[Lordamere Lake]], these fledgling spellcasters founded [[Dalaran]], the second Arathorian city-state.<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Guardians_of_Tirisfal The Guardians of Tirisfal]</ref>

During the following centuries, other city-states arose across the continent. Among them were the militaristic [[Gilneas (kingdom)|Gilneas]] and [[Alterac (kingdom)|Alterac]] (both strong supporters of the empire), whose mighty armies explored the mountainous southern lands of [[Khaz Modan]] and made first contact with the [[Dwarf|dwarves]]. On an [[Kul Tiras|island]] south of the imperial capital, [[Kul Tiras (kingdom)|Kul Tiras]] was built and developed a prosperous economy based fishing, shipping, and commerce. Meanwhile, Dalaran became the chief center of learning for magicians throughout the land. Although the four city-states had their own customs and commercial workings, they all held to the unifying authority of Strom, which acted as the central hub of the expansive empire.<ref name="TheSevenKingdoms">[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Seven_Kingdoms The Seven Kingdoms]</ref>

As the economy of Arathor flourished, its strongest elements began to disintegrate. The nobles of Strom, seeking lusher lands, purity, and enlightenment, decided to leave the arid surroundings of the imperial capital against the arguments of the royalty. Far to the north of Dalaran, the greater citizenry founded a city-state named [[Capital City|Lordaeron]], from which the [[Lordaeron|entire continent]] would take its name, which became a mecca for religious travelers and all those who sought inner peace and security.<ref name="TheSevenKingdoms" />

Left within the crumbling walls of ancient Strom, the Arathi descendants decided to travel south past the rocky Khaz Modan. After many long seasons of journey, they settled in the southern region of the continent they would name Azeroth and founded the kingdom of [[Stormwind (kingdom)|Stormwind]], which quickly became a self-sufficient power in its own right.<ref name="TheSevenKingdoms" />

Meanwhile, in the almost silent Strom, the few warriors still left decided to remain and guard the ancient walls of their city. As Strom was no longer the center of the empire, the soldiers developed it into a new martial nation known as [[Stromgarde (kingdom)|Stromgarde]]. Though each of the seven city-states became prosperous in its own right, the empire of Arathor had effectively disintegrated. As each nation developed its own customs and beliefs, they became increasingly segregated from one another and humanity lost the unity achieved during the rule of King Thoradin.<ref name="TheSevenKingdoms" />

Among the history books in [[Medivh]]'s [[Guardian's Library|library]], some mentioned references of genocides, assassinations, and massacres between humans of the seven kingdoms, using claims of nobility, heritage, and honor to justify their conflicts.<ref>''The Last Guardian''</ref>

The '''Shadowmoon clan''', also spelled '''Shadow Moon clan''',<ref name="WC2 Manual">''Warcraft II: Beyond the Dark Portal'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Beyond_the_Dark_Portal_manual#Shadow_Moon_Clan Clans of Draenor]'', Shadow Moon Clan</ref> is an orcish clan that was led by the orc shaman [[Ner'zhul]], and was the most powerful clan on [[Draenor]] prior to the world's destruction.

==History==
Much like all orcish clans at that time, the clan was very heavily influenced by shamanistic traditions. Although the Shadowmoon clan practiced traditional orc shamanism, their leader, Ner'zhul practiced a much darker version of shamanism, that was heavily influenced by Warlock magic, a result of Ner'zhul's trafficking with [[Kil'jaeden]], a demon of immense power. Kil'jaeden had the objective of turning the orcs into a Horde of blood-thirsty creatures to satisfy the Burning Legion, a powerful force bent on the destruction of various worlds in the Great Dark Beyond. Ner'zhul later realized what Kil'jaeden was doing, and attempted to halt the orcs' corruption. His efforts were in vain, as his own student, Gul'dan, continued Kil'jaeden's schemes to horrifying success.<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Kil%27jaeden_and_the_Shadow_Pact Kil'jaeden and the Shadow Pact]</ref>

Following the Horde's defeat on Azeroth at the end of the Second War, Ner'zhul rallied the clans still left on Draenor under his new banner. Aided by the Shadowmoon clan, he planned to open portals to new worlds for the orcs to conquer using four artifacts: the Skull of Gul'dan, the Jeweled Scepter of Sargeras, the Eye of Dalaran and the Book of Medivh.<ref name="The Invasion of Draenor">[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Invasion_of_Draenor The Invasion of Draenor]</ref> During this time, the Shadowmoon ruled over the scattered orcish clans, and Ner'zhul kept the other clans subjugated through fear and brute force.<ref name="WC2 Manual" />

After many battles with the [[Alliance Expedition]], Ner'zhul gathered some of the death knights and a number of Shadowmoon orcs to begin the Spell of Conjuration. Ner'zhul finally opened his portals to other worlds, but he did not foresee the terrible price he would pay. The portals' tremendous energies began to tear the very fabric of Draenor apart. Ner'zhul and his loyal Shadowmoon clan passed through the largest of the newly created portals, and shortly thereafter the world ripped apart.<ref name="The Invasion of Draenor" />

On the other side of the portal, Ner'zhul and his companions entered the Twisting Nether, where they were captured by Kil'jaeden. Kil'jaeden gruesomely tortured Ner'zhul for some time before remaking him into the spectral Lich King. His loyal death knights and Shadowmoon followers were also transformed by the demon's chaotic energies, being ripped apart and remade into skeletal liches to ensure that even in death, they would serve Ner'zhul unquestioningly.<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Birth_of_the_Lich_King The Birth of the Lich King]</ref><ref>''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Lich Undead Hero Units]'', Lich</ref>

The '''Shadow Council''' is a group of mortal [[warlock (lore)|warlock]]s that serve the [[demon]]s of the [[Burning Legion]].

== The First War ==
When the Demonlord [[Kil'jaeden]] was first in contact with the [[orc]]ish warlock [[Gul'dan]], he instructed the orc to form the Council in order to secretly rule the clans and spread the use of warlock magic.  In order to cement the Legion's control of the orcs, the Shadow Council summoned [[Mannoroth|Mannoroth the Destructor]], so that the clan chieftains could drink his blood, damning their race to decades of bloodlust.  Only [[Durotan]] of the [[Frostwolf]] clan refused.

[[Blackhand|Blackhand the Destroyer]] became [[warchief]] by the will of the Council, acting as their puppet in the conquests of Draenor and [[Stormwind]].  It was the warlocks of Shadow Council that created the Draenor side of the dimensional gateway known as the [[Dark Portal]].  

King [[Llane Wrynn]] was assassinated by one of the Shadow Council's finest killers: the half-orc, [[Garona]].  Following the death of [[Medivh]], [[Gul'dan]] was incapacitated for several weeks.  During this time, [[Orgrim Doomhammer]] killed Blackhand the Destroyer and seized the mantle of warchief.  He captured and tortured Garona to learn of the existence of the Shadow Council, and sensing it threatened his position, launched an attack on Gul'dan's citadel near the ruins of Stormwind, annihilating the warlocks of the Council.  Their spirits were subsequently imbued into the [[death knight (Second War)|death knight]]s.

==Beyond the Third War==
Even in the aftermath of the second invasion of the [[Burning Legion]], servants of the Shadow Council still remain. They now reside at [[Jaedenar]] in [[Felwood]].  The order now includes members of all races, provided they possess the ideology of acceptance of the tenets of the Burning Legion.  The hold of the Shadow Council is extensive; they control cell-based organizations throughout [[Kalimdor]] including the [[Burning Blade]] and [[Searing Blade Clan|Searing Blade]] cults. Agents of the Council have even infiltrated areas of the orcish capital city of [[Orgrimmar]].

At Jaedenar, deep within the ancient [[kaldorei]] structure that has been converted into the corrupt [[Shadow Hold]], Shadow Lord [[Fel'dan]] commanded the Council's demonic activities alongside his [[dreadlord]] advisor and liaison with the remnants of the Legion, the malevolent [[Lord Banehollow]]. However, agents of the organization known as the [[Emerald Circle]] were recently dispatched to Shadow Hold. Therein, they slew Fel'dan, along with his demonic slaves, and devastated much of the Shadow Council as well. It is strongly suspected that the power vacuum created by the Shadow Lord's death will cause infighting and turmoil within the ranks of the Shadow Council that may ultimately spell the doom of the organization.

'''Settlements''' are areas were people gather to live, going from small villages of a couple of dozens of people to bustling cities of thousands of souls.

==City==
{{maincat|Cities}}
''Cities'' are large settlements were people live that are usually much bigger than towns. Normally surrounded by tall walls, cities are protected by their own armies, especially if it is the [[capital]] of a [[nation]]. It has multiples services, though not always included in all cities, such as [[bank]]s, [[flight path]]s, [[inn]]s, [[auction house]]s and much more. As of patch 1.9.0, all faction capitals should have an [[auction house]].

In ''[[Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos|Warcraft III]]'' "Cityscape" is a tileset used in single-player and on custom maps.

==Village/Town==
{{maincat|Villages}}
[[File:Warcraft I - Town.jpg|thumb|200px]]
''Villages'' or ''towns'' are not large enough to be cities but they have a good amount of buildings and citizens. The distinction between a town and a small settlement can be fuzzy though towns usually have some vendors and flight paths but no banks or auction houses. Inns are often found in them, but it is not a guarantee. Settlements can be found along the roads toward raids, cities and other regions. Other names include ''hamlets'' etc. In human lands, its denizens are known as [[commoner|villagers]].

In ''[[Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos|Warcraft III]]'' "Village" and "Village Fall" are tilesets used in single-player and on custom maps.


==Camp==
{{maincat|Camps}}
''Camps'' are small settlements that lack any significant building, though they normally have a flight path. Sometimes, if they are big enough, camps can have [[forge]]s and other [[profession]] buildings. Lots of different races have camps scattered all around Azeroth. Other names include ''posts'', or ''forward camps''. [[Tent]]s may be used to set up a camp.
